To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
symbiotic endobions are a useful tool for reconstructing depositional environments of Silurian stromatoroporoids of Baltica.

the distribution of symbiotic stromatoporoid endobionts is related to different depositional environments and that the distribution of these endobionts was controlled by several environmental factors.

the distribution of symbiotic microendobionts in stromatoporoids from the Silurian (Ludlow–Pridoli) of Estonia is controlled by sedimentary facies and that the symbiotic microendobia are not only associated with shallow-water stromatoporoids, but are also found in deeper-water ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of endobiont communities in stromatoporoids, the environmental controls of their distribution and the palaeoecological significance of these communities.
the distribution of symbiotic organisms, their host stromatoporoids, and the sedimentological setting.

the distribution of symbiotic associations in Silurian shallow water stromatoporoids in the Silurina region of Estonia and the factors that may have influenced the distribution of symbiont associations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
symbiotic endobions were more diverse in the onshore shallow water facies, where stromatoporoid host species were more diverse and the stromatoporoid communities were more complex.
symbiotic endobions are not restricted to shallow water environments and that the symbiosis between stromatoporoids and their endobions is not restricted to shallow marine environments.

the symbiotic endobient associations in the studied stromatoporoids are not related to the depth of the depositional environment, but to the sedimentary facies and the distribution of the stromatoporoid host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
symbionts are not evenly distributed in the studied stromatoporoids but are concentrated in specific areas of the hosts.
the distribution of the endobionts is controlled by a number of factors, including substrate type, sedimentation rate, water depth and nutrient levels.
symbiotic endobiotic associations were not randomly distributed, but were controlled by environmental parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
symbiotic endobionic associations can be used as a proxy for the reconstruction of the palaeoecological conditions in the Silurinian of the Baltic palaeocontinent.
symbiotic endobioent associations can be used as a biostratigraphic marker in the Silurin of the Baltic region.
the distribution of endobionts can be used as a proxy for paleoenvironmental reconstructions.
